purpose: Danazol is used to treat endometriosis, a condition where tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus causing pain. It is also used for fibrocystic breast disease, which causes painful lumpy breasts, and for a rare condition called hereditary angioedema that causes episodes of severe swelling. It works by reducing the hormones that drive these conditions.
how_it_works: Danazol is a man-made hormone that acts like a weak male hormone (androgen) in your body. It works by lowering the levels of estrogen and progesterone, the female hormones that can feed conditions like endometriosis. By doing this, it helps shrink abnormal tissue and reduces pain and swelling.
common_side_effects: Weight gain, acne, oily skin, and unwanted hair growth on the face or body are common. You may also notice voice changes (deepening), hot flashes, vaginal dryness, mood changes, muscle cramps, and irregular or missed periods. Some people feel tired or notice swelling in their ankles.
warnings: Danazol can cause serious liver problems and should not be used if you are pregnant, as it can harm a baby and cause birth defects. It is not safe for people with heart, kidney, or liver disease. Use reliable non-hormonal birth control while taking it. Men and women should be aware it can cause masculinizing effects that may not fully reverse after stopping. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual weight gain, or severe headaches.
typical_dosing: The usual dose ranges from 100 mg to 800 mg per day, taken in two divided doses by mouth. Your doctor will start you on the right dose for your condition and may adjust it based on how you respond. Treatment for endometriosis usually lasts 3 to 6 months. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
